summary: Tested the new Cari Hesap Ekstresi (current accounts) feature end-to-end. Added 8 new backend regression tests in /app/backend/tests/test_current_accounts_regression.py covering POST/GET summaries & balance_after, pending-vs-completed cash effect on overview, PUT/DELETE adjusting overview without duplicate ledger rows, request_id idempotency + 409 conflict, person/currency filtering + chronological running balance, legacy /api/company/debts endpoints (including POST /debts/{id}/payments decorator intact), and 409 blocking when deleting a person with current entries (single + bulk). All 8 new tests pass. Re-ran the pre-existing company finance regression (13 tests) — all still pass. Frontend Playwright E2E on Cari Ekstre page covered: page renders with all required data-testids (current-accounts-page, current-entry-form, current-cash-effect, current-cash-status, current-summary-section, current-statement-table), Kişi Ekle dialog creates person and auto-selects, creating a payable movement with 'Kasadan çıkış' + 'Gerçekleşti' adds summary card + statement row, filter via summary card works, Eski Borç/Alacak tab mounts legacy Debts screen (2 forms visible), edit + delete flow works, and /company overview has 0px horizontal overflow at 390/768/1440 widths. Cleaned up all TEST_CARI_ fixtures from admin user as required.
critical_code_review_comments: treasury.company_overview adds current_cash_ledger entries using cents(entry['amount']) where entry['amount'] is already signed (negative for out). This happens to work because cents handles negatives, but it would be clearer to keep signed amounts in cents natively from current_cash_ledger_entries to avoid float->cents round-trip.

current_accounts.py update_current_entry allows setting request_id again via CurrentEntryIn (same model); frontend sends a new request_id on PUT. Backend ignores request_id uniqueness on update (writes it as 'id' only on insert) which is fine, but worth noting it is a soft contract.
routes.py bulk_delete_people uses await inside dict construction which is correct but very dense; consider refactoring for readability. Functionally verified to return 409 correctly.
